strategy.thesis: Very early-stage VC that writes the first institutional check into Israeli startups, often when there is just an idea, a little traction and a presentation. Founded by Lee Moser, former chief of staff to Israel's ambassador to the US.

summary.en: Tel Aviv early-stage VC founded in 2020 by Lee Moser (former chief of staff to Israeli ambassador Michael Oren); its $70M first fund backs Israeli startups at the idea/pre-seed stage.

sources.title: From the White House to a $30 million seed fund
sources.supports: Founded ~2020 by Lee Moser; very early-stage focus
sources.quote: Lee Moser left her previous position in early March 2020 to establish AnD Ventures

verification_notes: Founder Lee Moser later co-founded Protego Ventures (2024, defense). AnD's HQ is most often listed as Tel Aviv; some directory pages (Facebook) list Herzliya. strategy.thesis: Israel's first VC fund dedicated to gaming and gamification, investing globally in gaming studios and supporting technology. Led by former Google games-division executive Eitan Reisel.

summary.en: Israel's first gaming-dedicated VC, launched March 2020 by ex-Google games lead Eitan Reisel. Three funds totalling ~$343M; its $142M Fund III (Dec 2024) is its largest. 38 portfolio companies including SuperPlay and InnPlay Labs (both acquired by Playtika).

verification_notes: Fund I figures vary by source ($30M initial raise per the early Globes headline, $60m total per Dealroom). Fund II reported as $141M (Dec 2021).

strategy.thesis: First-check fund for 'pre-consensus' founders — backing unconventional entrepreneurs and problems considered too hard or markets considered too underserved for traditional early-stage VC; deliberately avoids crowded areas like cybersecurity.

summary.en: Tel Aviv pre-seed/seed fund established late 2021 by Fundbox co-founder Yuval Ariav. Its $50M debut fund (closed Aug 2023) writes first checks of $500K–$3.5M into unconventional 'pre-consensus' founders. Portfolio includes Sightful, Breeze, Nilus and Jiga.

sources.title: Symbol closes $50m debut Israel VC fund

sources.quote: Symbol closes $50m debut Israel VC fund ... investing between $500,000 and $3.5 million

verification_notes: Established late 2021; debut fund closed and announced August 2023. Plans 14–16 investments.

strategy.thesis: Early-stage deep-tech VC focused on cybersecurity, AI infrastructure, developer tools and digital health, plus frontier areas such as quantum, space tech, neuroscience and synthetic biology.

summary.en: Early-stage deep-tech VC co-founded by Gadi Isaev and Rafael Gold; its $15M Fund I began operating in 2021 and a $25M Fund II launched in 2025. Focuses on cybersecurity, AI infrastructure, digital health and frontier tech.

sources.supports: Fund I $15M (2021), Fund II $25M, founders, check size up to $1M, sector focus

strategy.thesis: Pre-seed, seed and opportunistic Series A fund co-founded by former NBA player Omri Casspi and veteran early-stage investor David Citron; plans ~20 investments of $1M–$2M each.

summary.en: Tel Aviv early-stage fund launched early 2022 by ex-NBA player Omri Casspi and VC David Citron. $50M target ($30M raised), writing $1M–$2M checks into ~20 fintech, cybersecurity and web3 startups.

sources.supports: Fund target $50M ($30M raised), founders, founded early 2022, check size, planned 20 investments, sectors

verification_notes: Co-founder David Citron later left to launch TBD VC (2025). Sheva began operating at the beginning of 2022.

strategy.thesis: Growth-stage fund founded by three former Goldman Sachs Israel executives, investing in Israeli and European tech companies with proven technology and tens of millions in revenue, near acquisition or IPO. Focus on AI infrastructure, mission-critical software and defense.

summary.en: Herzliya-based $300M growth-equity fund launched in 2022 by three former Goldman Sachs Israel executives (Sarel Eldor, Danny Akerman, Amit Pilowsky). Backs late-stage Israeli and European tech companies nearing exit.

sources.title: Former Goldman Sachs execs launching $300 million tech growth fund

verification_notes: HQ in Herzliya (a distinct municipality north of Tel Aviv within the Tel Aviv District) — qualifies as a non-hub-city fund. Announced January 2022.

strategy.thesis: Founded in the wake of the October 7, 2023 attacks to ensure continuity for viable Israeli startups; invests across sectors including defense tech, medtech and deep tech, targeting scale-up-ready companies and helping them enter the US market. Partnership with the State of Indiana ($15M commitment).

summary.en: Tel Aviv VC set up in October 2023 in response to the October 7 attacks to support Israeli startups; later expanded into a full-scale fund. $60M ($50M raised), investing seed–Series B across deep/defense/medtech and helping companies access the US market. Notable: Illumex (acquired by Nvidia).

verification_notes: Founders Gil Friedlander and Chen Linchevski also linked to Calyx Ventures. Began as an emergency impact fund Oct 2023, later expanded into a full VC fund with the $60M vehicle.

current_fund.raw: many tens of millions of dollars (undisclosed)

strategy.thesis: Investment vehicle formed by leading cybersecurity entrepreneurs pooling their own capital to support Israeli high-tech companies amid the wartime funding downturn, providing both capital and deep cyber domain expertise.

summary.en: Cyber-focused fund formed February 2024 by veteran cybersecurity entrepreneurs (Mickey Boodaei, Rakesh Loonkar, Dan Amiga, Mike Fey) pooling tens of millions of their own money to back Israeli tech during the wartime downturn. Early investment: Cortanix.

Founders are partners in/founders of cyber companies (Trusteer, Transmit Security, Island, McAfee/Symantec).

strategy.thesis: Dedicated defense and national-security technology fund investing in early- and growth-stage companies developing AI, autonomous systems, robotics and advanced sensing, as wars in Ukraine and the Middle East accelerate demand for defense tech.

summary.en: Israel's defense and national-security tech fund, founded 2024 by Lital Leshem and Lee Moser (the only Israeli defense-tech fund led by two women). $150M target; raised $70M in two weeks and expected to close near $200M. Focus on AI, autonomous systems, robotics and advanced sensing.

strategy.thesis: Defense-tech fund targeting defense-sector startups and dual-use technologies for both defense and civilian markets, founded by former senior Israeli intelligence and Air Force figures together with MizMaa venture capitalists.

verification_notes: Launched as part of the post-October-7 wave of Israeli defense-tech funds (raising during 2024–2025). Exact founding date not stated; HQ not explicitly confirmed but team is Israel-based.

strategy.thesis: Backs deep-tech Israeli founders at pre-seed and seed in cybersecurity, enterprise software and technical infrastructure, with support from venture partners at major tech companies. Commits to donating fund profits to the Back the Warrior nonprofit.

summary.en: Tel Aviv pre-seed/seed fund launched April 2025 by David Citron (ex-Sheva) and Alan Buch, born from a chance reunion at the Zikim Gaza-border crossing during the war. $35M fund writing ~$1M checks into ~20 Israeli deep-tech/cyber/enterprise startups.

strategy.thesis: Israel's first VC fund dedicated exclusively to quantum computing, backing 12–15 early-stage hardware and software startups in the quantum field from pre-seed to Series A.

people.role: Co-Founder & General Partner (former CTO, Check Point)

strategy.thesis: Deep-tech fund backing companies from post-research to commercial breakthrough in quantum computing, AI infrastructure, advanced energy and robotics — addressing bottlenecks (energy, compute, manpower) in the AI super-cycle, with emphasis on US–Israel cooperation.

summary.en: US–Israel deep-tech fund (offices Tel Aviv, NY, LA) launched ~2025/2026 by Lior Prosor and Michael Broukhim, chaired by Eclipse Ventures founder Lior Susan. $150M ($100M first close) for quantum, AI infrastructure, advanced energy and robotics.

strategy.thesis: Israeli deep-tech venture arm of Igor Tulchinsky's WorldQuant (~$30B AUM hedge-fund group), investing in early-stage Israeli deep-tech companies at the intersection of AI, robotics and biotechnology; targets 2–3 investments per year of up to $1M.

summary.en: Ramat Gan deep-tech venture arm of Igor Tulchinsky's WorldQuant, launched 2026 and run by Maj. Gen. (res.) Saar Tzur. Invests up to $1M into 2–3 early-stage Israeli AI/robotics/biotech companies per year; first deal Navairo (counter-drone).

strategy.thesis: Haifa-based early-stage VC dedicated to backing startups founded by Israeli-Arab entrepreneurs, providing funding, office space, research assistance and professional networks to address the under-representation of Arab founders in Israel's tech sector.

summary.en: Haifa-based VC (founded 2015) dedicated to Israeli-Arab founders, co-founded by Imad Telhami with backing from JVP's Erel Margalit and Pitango's Chemi Peres. Its second fund (Takwin 2, 2022) targets $80M. Included for the segment's non-hub-city criterion (Haifa, not Tel Aviv).

strategy.thesis: Government incentive program (a revival of the original 1990s Yozma) run by the Israel Innovation Authority: the state contributes 30 cents per institutional dollar invested in Israeli VC funds (and waives its share of returns) to raise local capital's share of Israeli high-tech and reduce dependence on foreign capital.

summary.en: A 2024 Israel Innovation Authority program reviving the historic Yozma model: government adds $0.30 per institutional $1 invested into Israeli VC funds, aiming to channel ~$1B/year (2024–2026) and ~$4B leveraged. First round allocated $155M to 18 institutional entities and was oversubscribed by ~$474M.
